key_insight: The paper proves that a standard mesh-free discretization of a nonlinear bond-based peridynamic fracture model converges for a fixed horizon, even with irreversible bond breakage.
engineering_relevance: This gives mathematical assurance that common peridynamic fracture simulations can be trusted at the discretization level before studying the more difficult zero-horizon limit.
method: Analyze a well-posed regularized dynamic peridynamic model with tension-driven bond breakage.
Include the practical one-point quadrature used in mesh-free schemes directly in the convergence proof.
Establish convergence in C^1([0,T], L^\infty(Ω)^d) and derive local Lipschitz bounds for the displacement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a convergence proof based on the natural solution norm and derives spatial regularity bounds for locally L-Lipschitz input data.
watch_item: The result is for a fixed horizon δ > 0 only, so it does not address the physically important limit as δ approaches 0.
paper_title: On the Convergence of the Mesh-Free Discretization of a Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model with a Bond-Breakage Criterion
